strategies.name: continuation
strategies.description: General continuation logic: trade with established structure only after location and momentum stop fighting the idea.
conditions: Trend structure is clear (HH/HL for buys or LH/LL for sells)
strategies.good_example: HH/HL uptrend, price pulls back into structure, momentum turns back up, spread is acceptable.
strategies.bad_example: Price is in the middle of a range or chop while momentum is weak/mixed.
strategies.operator_teaching_prompt: If Atlas holds in mid-range chop, that may be correct. If it holds after clean pullback confirmation, label it too_cautious or missed_trade.
strategies.notes: Continuation seeks follow-through, not reversal guessing.

strategies.name: trend_continuation
strategies.good_example: Directional structure is mature but not exhausted, session is liquid, and confirmation appears near a reaction zone.
strategies.bad_example: Trend exists, but entry is late after expansion or against conflicting DXY/US10Y pressure.
strategies.operator_teaching_prompt: Teach Atlas whether the hold was patient or late by labeling correct_hold versus missed_trade.

strategies.name: breakout_retest
strategies.good_example: Break, retest, hold, and renewed momentum with acceptable spread.
strategies.bad_example: First candle through a level with no retest, weak follow-through, or poor liquidity.
strategies.operator_teaching_prompt: If Atlas wants to chase the first break, label bad_setup. If it waits for a retest and the break runs without retest, label missed_trade only if context was clean.

strategies.name: liquidity_sweep_reversal
strategies.good_example: Prior high/low is swept, wick rejects quickly, structure reclaims, and reversal momentum confirms.
strategies.bad_example: A wick appears but price does not reclaim structure or momentum remains with the old direction.
strategies.operator_teaching_prompt: Teach Atlas that sweep alone is not enough. Use correct_hold when it avoids an unconfirmed reversal.

strategies.name: range_mean_reversion
strategies.good_example: Defined range, price rejects the edge, trend strength is weak, and entry is not mid-range.
strategies.bad_example: Price is in the middle of the range or range boundary is not clear.
strategies.operator_teaching_prompt: Use correct_hold for mid-range avoidance. Use missed_trade only when a defined edge rejection was present and execution friction was acceptable.

operator_teaching_labels.correct_hold: Atlas avoided a low-quality or unsafe moment.
operator_teaching_labels.too_cautious: Atlas held even though setup, location, context, and execution conditions were clean.
operator_teaching_labels.missed_trade: Atlas failed to act on a high-quality opportunity that matched its own playbook and gates.
operator_teaching_labels.bad_setup: Atlas liked or nearly liked a setup that was structurally poor.
operator_teaching_labels.execution_issue: The idea was acceptable but broker, spread, slippage, or session execution quality was the problem.
operator_teaching_labels.confusing_answer: Atlas' explanation was unclear, irrelevant, or not grounded in the actual question.

strategy_framework.signal_generation: Strategies produce directional candidates with confidence and risk parameters.
strategy_framework.filtering: Candidates are filtered by regime, liquidity, spread, session, and safety constraints.
strategy_framework.selection: Final choice depends on confidence, context alignment, and risk-policy guards.

risk_policy_alignment.paper_first: Operational changes are validated in paper/demo mode before any live consideration.
risk_policy_alignment.guardrails: Consecutive-loss, drawdown, and trade-frequency controls are mandatory safety layers.
risk_policy_alignment.comparison_validation: Control-vs-experiment comparison is required before promoting changes.
